payload.headline: Tech keeps sliding; trend, fear and thin breadth still say stand aside

summary.thesis: Both SPY and QQQ are in downtrends, below their 50- and 200-day averages. Fear is 'elevated' as of Nov 24, and breadth is 8%. Trend, fear and breadth all point the same way.
summary.decision: Stand aside for new buying, both long-term and swing.
summary.act_at: A QQQ close above 682.54, its 200-day average and the market gate, ends the tech downtrend. A QQQ close below 608.45 or an SPY close below 689.81 would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline would be continuing.

payload.happening: SPY closed at 716.7, down 0.29% from 718.78. It is down 1.85% over 5 days and 7.2% over 20 days. QQQ closed at 633.93, down 0.65% from 638.1. It is down 3.88% over 5 days and 12.63% over 20 days. Both peaked for the month on Oct 28, at 772.31 for SPY and 725.61 for QQQ. Both hit their 1-month lows on Nov 20, at 689.81 and 608.45. The past year's highest closes were on Oct 6: 779.09 for SPY and 759.66 for QQQ. Q3 GDP (second estimate) with corporate profits, and October Personal Income and Outlays (including PCE inflation), were scheduled for today at 08:30. Their results are not in DATA, and no news was recorded since the last note.
payload.business: Trend: both indexes sit below their 50-day averages (SPY 757.85, QQQ 707.02) and their 200-day averages (SPY 730.77, QQQ 682.54), so the trend is down. Tech is weaker than the broad market. QQQ is 7.7% below its 200-day average, while SPY is 2.0% below its own. Fear: the VIX reading is in the 'elevated' band (20–30) and sits at the 95 percentile of its 252-day range. That reading is from Nov 24, because the Nov 25 value isn't stored yet. (General knowledge: the VIX reflects the market swings options traders expect over the next month.) Breadth: only 8% of stocks are above their 50-day averages, so the selling is broad, not limited to a few big names. Taken together, the market is falling, falling widely, and nervous. None of the three readings supports new buying yet. Both indexes are still above their Nov 20 lows: QQQ is 4.0% above and SPY is 3.8% above, so that floor is holding for now.

worth.text: This is a market note. No valuation is implied, and the levels below are price-trend markers only.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: Both indexes are still above their Nov 20 1-month lows (QQQ 608.45, SPY 689.81), so the recent low is holding.
SPY is only 2.0% below its 200-day average of 730.77, much closer to its long-term trend line than QQQ is to its own.

Breadth at 8% and a VIX reading at the 95 percentile mean the readings are stretched. (General knowledge: readings this stretched have sometimes come near short-term turning points, but they do not mark one by themselves.)
bear: QQQ is 7.7% below its 200-day average and 11.5% below its 50-day average, so tech is in a downtrend on both time frames.
Breadth fell from 10% in the last note to 8%, so fewer stocks are holding up.
Fear is still 'elevated' and up 0.9 over 5 days as of Nov 24. Both indexes fell again today, and QQQ is down 12.63% over 20 days.

levels.what: QQQ 200-day average and the market gate. A close above it ends the tech downtrend, which would support moving to a selective stance.
QQQ 1-month low (Nov 20). A close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline would be continuing.
QQQ 50-day average. A close above it would put tech's short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's 'QQQ above its 50-day average' check.
QQQ 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean the tech pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 1-month low (Nov 20). A close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline would be continuing.
SPY 200-day average. A close above it would put the broad market's long-term trend back up.
SPY 50-day average. A close above it would put SPY's short-term trend back up.
SPY 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean SPY's pullback is fully recovered.

longterm.why: QQQ closed at 633.93, 7.7% below its 200-day gate of 682.54. Fear is 'elevated' as of Nov 24, and breadth is 8%. Trend, fear and breadth all argue against new buying until QQQ closes above 682.54.

swing.why: QQQ is 11.5% below its 50-day average of 707.02. Below that level, setups keep failing the pipeline's market check, and today's 0.65% drop moved it further away.

decision.timing: Today's 08:30 releases (Q3 GDP second estimate with corporate profits, and October Personal Income and Outlays with PCE) are not reflected in DATA beyond the schedule. The jobs report is due Dec 4 at 08:30. The fear reading is from Nov 24 because the Nov 25 VIX isn't stored yet. The nearest levels to watch are SPY 730.77 above and 689.81 below, and QQQ 682.54 above and 608.45 below. The 50- and 200-day averages move every day, while the 1-month high and low are fixed past prices.

change_mind: A QQQ close above 682.54, its 200-day average and the market gate, would end the tech downtrend and support a move to selective. An SPY close above 730.77 would add confirmation for the broad market.
A QQQ close below 608.45 or an SPY close below 689.81 would set new 1-month lows, meaning the decline would be continuing and the stand-aside view gets stronger.
payload.what_changed: The stance is unchanged from Nov 24: stand aside on both horizons. QQQ fell from 638.1 to 633.93, and SPY fell from 718.78 to 716.7. Breadth slipped from 10% to 8%. The fear reading moved to Nov 24 (26.36, previously 26.62), still 'elevated'. The moving gates shifted slightly: QQQ's 200-day average went from 682.42 to 682.54 and its 50-day from 708.42 to 707.02. SPY's 200-day average went from 730.62 to 730.77 and its 50-day from 758.56 to 757.85. The 1-month lows (608.45, 689.81) and highs (725.61, 772.31) are unchanged.
